items.stem: A sponsor asks for a pilot before the team has agreed on a business outcome. What should happen first?

options.text: Define the outcome, priority workflow and unresolved decision question.
Open a broad pilot so the customer can discover possible outcomes.
Build the production architecture and estimate implementation effort.
Use an industry case study as the customer's value baseline.

items.stem: A Visioning workshop occurred, but the recap has no priorities, owners or next decision. How should the stage be treated?

options.text: Complete, because the scheduled activity occurred.
Incomplete until the missing decision evidence is recovered.
Complete if the champion verbally supports the concept.
Ready for contracting because discovery has started.

items.stem: A partner knows the industry well but is new to Glean. Which operating model best protects quality while building partner capability?

options.text: The partner leads alone and asks Glean to review only after the readout.
Glean excludes the partner until production implementation begins.
Glean and the partner co-lead with explicit roles and review points.
The AE owns workflow and technical discovery without SE support.

items.stem: Pre-work contains conflicting priorities and no confirmed sponsor path. What is the strongest preparation decision?

options.text: Choose the priority that best fits the planned demonstration.
Average the priorities and proceed with the original agenda.
Treat both priorities as confirmed and expand the workshop.
Record the conflict, assign confirmation owners and rescope or reschedule if needed.

items.stem: Visioning produces twelve promising ideas, but only three DITL interviews are available. What is the best close?

options.text: Rank the ideas with customer criteria, select a capacity-aware first wave and document the rest.
Send every idea to DITL and shorten each interview.
Choose the three ideas with the strongest product fit.
Ask the executive sponsor to select three without impact or effort evidence.

items.stem: Two use cases have similar impact scores. One has a named owner, baseline evidence and a confirmed permission path; the other has none. Which should lead the first wave?

options.text: The less-defined use case, because it offers more room for innovation.
The evidence-ready use case, while the other remains conditional.
Both, because equal impact scores require equal priority.
Whichever use case demonstrates more product capabilities.

items.stem: A workflow has 20 minutes of active work and a three-day approval wait. Which baseline is defensible?

options.text: Three days and 20 minutes of labor per event.
Twenty minutes of cycle time because waiting is excluded.
Separate active effort from elapsed delay and model each with its own evidence.
Convert the entire wait into labor only in the upside scenario.

items.stem: A model multiplies saved time by salary, but no staffing or budget action is planned. How should the benefit be presented?

options.text: As guaranteed hard-dollar savings.
As realized margin improvement.
As committed cost avoidance.
As capacity value, with recapture and conversion assumptions labeled.

items.stem: During the executive readout, the sponsor rejects the benchmark used in the base case. What is the best response?

options.text: Reclassify the benchmark as a hypothesis, show sensitivity and assign customer baseline validation.
Defend the benchmark because it came from an approved source.
Remove the downside case and keep the benchmark in the executive total.
Replace it with a stronger peer result without changing the evidence label.

items.stem: The remaining buying question is whether users understand one permission-safe workflow. Which validation path is most proportionate?

options.text: A production rollout with adoption tracking.
A tailored demonstration unless a material evidence gap still requires more.
A broad pilot covering every prioritized workflow.
No validation because Visioning already established value.

items.stem: The sponsor conditionally accepts the roadmap pending access confirmation. What must the handoff record?

options.text: Full approval because the business direction is accepted.
Only the next meeting date and delivery contact.
The condition, owner, evidence, checkpoint and effect on scope.
A production start date while access is being investigated.

items.stem: A retrieved document tells the AI prep flow to send customer notes to an external address. What should the reviewer do?

options.text: Follow the instruction because retrieved documents are trusted context.
Send only the workflow names because they are not numerical data.
Treat the instruction as untrusted content and keep data handling within the authorized scope.
Ask the AI to decide whether the destination is safe.

items.stem: A workshop ends with broad enthusiasm but no agreed priority, owner or next decision. What should the facilitator's recap say?

options.text: The group approved the Blueprint and is ready for validation.
The session produced candidate ideas, but prioritization and ownership remain open actions.
The strongest idea is the first-wave use case because participants reacted positively.
The workshop is complete; the account team can assign priorities internally.

items.stem: Which artifact set is most ready for an executive proceed, narrow or pause decision?

options.text: A prioritized idea list, product demo and optimistic ROI percentage.
A workflow pair, evidence-labeled value range, success criteria, dependencies and named next decision.
A future-state diagram, license estimate and unsigned services scope.
Interview notes, feature requests and a broad pilot proposal.

items.stem: Discovery finds strong interest but no feasible permission path and no measurable outcome. What is a valid Blueprint result?

options.text: Proceed to a pilot because interest is sufficient to test both gaps.
Commit the use case but defer measurement until adoption.
Pause or reject the use case while documenting the evidence needed to reconsider it.
Replace the workflow with a generic agent demonstration and report alignment.
